name: Tryout
why: Borrowing a shop member's On Recruit is a neat shop read, but the payoff is whatever the row happens to hold.

name: Gather
why: Same shape as Stash and Allowance word for word; plain fuel with a small recruit bonus, nobody notices it.

name: Walk-In
why: Blind top-of-pile recruit is red's one allowed gamble, and feeding every rival 1 red is a nice table gift.

name: Promote
why: Trading up into a rival's better member is a real aim-and-pick turn that a trailing player can use to grab a leader's engine.

name: Demote
why: Mirror of Promote; trading down is mostly for dumping a weak card, so it fires less often and feels smaller.

name: Initiation
why: A free recruit up to 8 in round III is a big clean burst anyone behind can grab.

name: Body Snatchers
why: Every Round Start you pick a rival's same-cost member to swap; real aiming, and Loyalists answers it.

name: Volunteer
why: Cost-1 filler worth 1; its only job is feeding recruit triggers and red's count, nothing fires.

name: Mentor & Protégés
why: Two members for one buy, a free cheapest-recruit that stacks with Proselytizers and Recruiter.

name: Proselytizers
why: Simple recruit trigger that turns red's many free recruits into steady followers.

name: Mob
why: Up to +6 a round for the red leader only; pure rich-get-richer at cost 12 that nobody can Promote away.

name: Recruiter
why: Recruit refund that keeps red's free-recruit turns fuelled; small but it stacks.

name: Patriarch
why: Generic game-end scorer that works the same in any wide cult; nobody reacts.

name: Foster Parents
why: Pays off exactly what Promote, Demote, Body Snatchers and Poach already do; a clean connector.

name: Deprogrammers
why: Worth 4 for 3 cost is the real draw; the -1 follower sting on swaps is small and visible.

name: Panel
why: Promote or Demote packed into a recruit; plays off red's own spaces, needs those spaces known.

name: Loyalists
why: Clean shield against red's swaps; switches off a whole kind of answer for its owner's cult.

name: Clerk
why: Flat +1 red each round: forgettable, nothing to decide, no link to any red card.

name: Sleep In
why: Big purple now for a slower next turn; a real tempo trade on the Goes Last token.

name: Hold Up
why: Skipping whoever is next, even yourself, is a funny snake read the whole table watches.

name: Right Away
why: Small purple plus a double turn; clean and fires Courier and Hot Streak.

name: Last Call
why: Rewards holding minions and going last, a real round II plan; wording of the token step is heavy.

name: Crunch Time
why: Three turns in a row is a big snake bend in five words; a trailing player can grab spaces before rivals.

name: Overtime
why: An extra minion in round III is a clear burst for anyone.

name: Courier
why: Turns purple's double turns into rainbow income; links Right Away, Crunch Time and Yellow sets.

name: Night Watch
why: Pays when rivals take Goes Last, but 'per minion on it' reads oddly cold.

name: Night Owls
why: A bonus minion every round from II is a clear rule bend, pricey at 8.

name: Early Birds
why: Simple immunity to Hold Up and Bouncers; matters only if those are out.

name: Bouncers
why: Two skipped rival turns on recruit is a loud tempo hit with a timing choice; Early Birds answers it.

name: Gossip
why: Rides on Hold Up and Bouncers, a clean payoff for the skip package.

name: Timekeeper
why: Count-your-color scorer, same shape as Snobs and Old Money; quiet.

name: Closer
why: Pays for winning the went-last race; ties straight to the purple contest.

name: Hot Streak
why: Big payoff for chaining Crunch Time and Right Away; the count of turns in a row is easy to lose at a table.

name: Picket Line
why: Passive +1 purple when rivals visit purple; same shape as High Society, nothing to decide.

name: Bell Ringer
hardFail: needs tracking a table can't do: whether the token was placed before the skip and whose turn was second in a row
why: Nested conditions nobody can read cold or track, all for +1 purple.

name: Toast
why: Big silver with a gift to rivals that feeds the most-silver contest; a real tension.

name: Polish
why: Simple 2-for-4 conversion; useful but fixes rather than excites.

name: Party Gifts
why: Pay rivals to gain followers, a clean give-to-get choice that powers Caterer and the silver contest race.

name: Potluck
hardFail: turn flow: asks rivals to choose during another player's turn
why: Every rival picks a resource to hand over during your turn; small and slows the table.

name: Sweet Talk
why: Silver plus conversion; overlaps Polish and Makeover.

name: Largesse
why: Up to 10 followers for gifting silver in round III; a big, readable finisher that also moves the silver contest.

name: Godparent
why: Give away a member for its cost in followers once; the gift and the timing make it a clean silver idea.

name: Hostesses
why: Automatic gift-for-followers each round; on rails.

name: Caterer
why: Pays off every gift card; 'gifted' leaves unclear whether rivals' gifts count.

name: Guest of Honor
why: Hands a cheap member away for +4 on silver turns; a real gift decision tied to red's Foster Parents.

name: Toastmaster
why: Cheap +1 follower per silver visit; fine filler, nothing to decide.

name: Debutantes
why: Doubling your silver is a big timed moment for the silver contest; rivals get a little.

name: Smooth Talkers
why: Silver as wild pay is a clean rule bend, expensive at 11.

name: Philanthropist
why: A small Party Gifts on recruit; repeats the color's spaces.

name: Creditor
why: Two followers from a rival each round, paid back in silver; strong every round and the target is singled out.

name: Debt Collectors
why: One-time 2 silver from each rival; plain take that fights its own gift theme.

name: High Society
why: Passive follower when rivals visit silver; mild reason to avoid silver.

name: Envy
hardFail: relies on a rival having more resources than you (most silver a rival holds minus yours)
why: Pays only when a rival out-holds you, and the math is hidden.

name: Harvest
why: Plain fuel space in chosen colors; the color's anchor.

name: Leaders' Tax
why: Reads where rivals' minions sit; a clean table read that pays more in a crowded color.

name: New Blood
why: Rewards a new color recruit; fits yellow's breadth.

name: Housewarming
why: A free new-color recruit up to 5; big and on theme.

name: Melting Pot
why: Scales with how wide your cult is; links to Drifters and Big Tent.

name: Makeover
why: Rearrange everything into sets for the full-sets contest; clean round III fixer.

name: Gardeners
why: Fills missing colors, which helps a broke player most.

name: Duty Collector
why: Passive tax on rivals' recruits in your colors; mild interaction.

name: Tourist
why: Followers per color held each round; rewards keeping a rainbow instead of spending it.

name: Seamstress
why: Doubling full sets is a big timed moment, but what 'double your sets' gives you needs explaining.

name: Dyer
why: Yellow per color held, scales a little; autopilot buy.

name: Meddler
why: Swapping one of each rival's resources can wreck set counts, but it's fiddly to resolve.

name: Drifters
why: Pick its color to fill a set, win the red count or feed Big Tent; a cheap flexible connector.

name: Big Tent
why: Rewards one of each color, a clear game-long plan that pushes against stacking.

name: Caravan
why: A rainbow every round is a strong engine, priced high.

name: Jack-of-All-Trades
why: Yellow as wild in sets; simple fix that sharpens the yellow contest.

name: Savings
why: Plain blue with a small shop dig.

name: Out of Style
why: Clearing a whole color from the shop is a loud deny move rivals feel.

name: Peek
why: Stack the pile and recruit from it; good blue tool, a little slow to resolve.

name: Recruit Twice
why: Two buys in one turn is a clean rule bend.

name: Bury
why: Deny a member and get half its cost; a modest deny pick.

name: Spree
why: Three buys in round III, a burst a trailing player can grab.

name: Hawker
hardFail: turn flow: asks rivals to choose during another player's turn
why: Each rival decides whether to buy during your turn; good auction idea, but breaks turn flow.

name: Patroness
why: Pays on every bottom-of-pile move, linking Bury, Out of Style and Window Shopper.

name: Snobs
why: Count-your-color scorer; quiet.

name: Window Shopper
why: Churns the shop and pays in its colors; feeds Patroness.

name: Shopaholics
why: Two buys every turn is a huge clean rule bend; priced high.

name: Window Dressers
why: Cheap body that resets the shop once; the reset helps nobody in particular.

name: Doormen
why: Swap a rival's member for a shop one every round; strong and fiddly cost rule.

name: Regular
why: Refund on follower buys; nothing blue about it and nobody notices.

name: Trendsetters
why: Each recruit also churns the shop; feeds Patroness.

name: Critic
why: Pays when rivals buy blue; cheap and makes rivals think.

name: Scavenger
hardFail: turn flow: asks rivals to choose during another player's turn
why: Owner decides to recruit on a rival's turn, an extra buy off their turn.

name: Help Yourself
why: A split steal you aim; the magenta core.

name: Stash
why: Copy of Gather and Allowance in magenta; nothing about stealing.

name: Lie Low
why: Small steal plus a round of safety; a real defend-or-attack call.

name: Heist
why: Steal 3 followers straight from the leader, catch-up in four words.

name: Shake Down
hardFail: turn flow: asks rivals to choose during another player's turn
why: Victim picks their own punishment on your turn; feels bad.

name: Poach
why: Take any rival member free in round III; huge, aimed and a real catch-up tool.

name: Cutpurse
hardFail: relies on a rival having more resources (targets the rival with the most resources)
why: Auto-steal from the richest; target set by rival holdings.

name: Accomplice
why: Cheap steal 3 on recruit; plain and punchy.

name: Grifter
why: Steal grows with your cult; scales with red and blue width.

name: Second-Story Man
why: Steal 2 right before contests, timed to flip a lead; a sharp aim choice.

name: Desperado
why: Makes every steal bigger while you trail; real catch-up.

name: Extortionist
hardFail: relies on a rival having more resources (targets the rival with the most resources)
why: Bigger Cutpurse with the same rival-holdings target.

name: Bodyguards
why: Full theft immunity; clear but switches off magenta against you.

name: Double Agent
why: Give it away and take one of theirs; reads like red's Promote, not a steal.

name: Kidnapper
why: Takes a member from the widest cult every round with no answer; the victim feels robbed.

name: Shoplifter
why: Steal 1 per recruit; small steady engine.

name: Fence
why: Punishes stealing from you; a soft deterrent.

name: Allowance
why: Third copy of the Gather shape; nothing white about it.

name: Splurge
why: Followers for spending big on a member; doubled rate in round II is a step to recall.

name: Exchange
why: Resources into followers at 2 each; steady white conversion.

name: Farewell
why: Cast out a member for its cost in followers; white's idea in one move, pairs with Martyrs.

name: Estate Sale
why: Farewell for white instead of followers; repeats its sibling.

name: Cash In
why: All white into followers in round III; the payoff Heiresses and Misers build to.

name: Recluse
why: Pays for staying small against wide rivals; catch-up for the narrow cult.

name: Landlord
why: Flat +2 white; forgettable.

name: Heiresses
why: Once per game white per member, set up for Cash In; a timed combo.

name: Brokers
why: +1 on every white follower payout; stacks with Exchange and Farewell.

name: Misers
why: Hold white for game-end points, a hold-or-cash call against Cash In.

name: Raiders
why: Steal 4 followers once, paid in white; strong but reads like magenta.

name: Cashier
why: A Cash In on recruit; timing it is the fun.

name: Money Changers
why: White whenever anyone buys followers; passive and mild.

name: Martyrs
why: Pays its cost when it leaves; turns Farewell, Promote and Poach into gains.

name: Old Money
why: Count-your-color scorer; quiet.

name: Hoarder
why: All resources into white once, setting up Cash In or Misers.

name: Build Up
why: Green's plain fuel anchor.

name: Echo
why: Copy the previous action; plays off whatever the table just did.

name: Reprise
why: Repeat your own space; solid.

name: Sample
why: Borrow a rival member's On Recruit; pick the best one on the table.

name: Cover
why: Copy an untaken action; clean.

name: Greatest Hits
why: Replay all your On Recruits in round III; rewards the cult you built.

name: Song Request
why: Copy a rival's space once a round; good table read.

name: Impersonator
why: Borrow a rival member's ability until you re-choose; strong but needs a marker to track.

name: Impressionist
why: Pays when anyone copies; cheap.

name: Wallflower
why: Doubles resources from copies; strong engine piece.

name: Fan Club
why: Copy the leader's space on recruit; catch-up.

name: Roadie
why: Scales with green members; autopilot.

name: Stunt Double
why: Copy the action you just took on recruit; simple.

name: Tribute Band
why: Do all of a rival's actions once; big but 14 cost.

name: Doppelganger
why: Become a copy of your best member; clean.

name: Agents
why: Rivals can't copy you; shuts off green.

name: Encore
why: Next On Recruit twice; a timing call.

name: Party Crasher
why: Place on a taken space once; bends the blocking rule.

name: Alchemists
why: All resources wild for recruits; a strong fixer.

name: Extra Hand
why: One extra minion for 9; pricey.

name: Line Cutters
why: Always first; cheap and loud for 2.

name: Old Maid
why: A poison card to pass with swaps; fun with red.

name: Dabblers
why: Counts double for member counts.

name: Anarchist
why: Swap any two members each round; powerful and swingy.

name: Spoilsport
why: Cancel one contest a round; denies the leader.

name: Con Men
why: Steal 5 on recruit; plain.

name: Sore Loser
why: Steal 5 followers from the contest leader if you win none; catch-up.
